title: Teen Left Stranded on a Cliff After Letting AI Plan Hike
source_used: CTV News (6 Oct 2026, article text read from the page; direct interview with the rescue team); Gizmodo (full text from the fulltext folder, which relays North Shore News)
key_facts: A 16-year-old solo hiker was rescued over the weekend from the base of the final headwall of the 'Widowmaker' climbing route on Crown Mountain, near Grouse Mountain north of Vancouver (CTV News says Sunday; Gizmodo, citing North Shore News, says Saturday).
North Shore Rescue was called at about 3:30 p.m.; two rescue technicians were lowered from a helicopter to the area and he was extracted by about 6:30 p.m.

CTV News, citing search manager Paul Markey: the teenager rode the gondola up Grouse Mountain at about 8 a.m. and asked Claude AI to plan a trip to Crown Mountain; it sent him via Crown Pass, Crater Slabs and Crown Couloir before the instructions led him off the trail route. Gizmodo says it is unclear which AI tool he used.
Markey: a fall 'would have resulted in significant injury or potentially death'; he urged hikers not to follow AI directions when mapping routes.
The teen had a lot of high-difficulty indoor climbing experience and came well equipped for hiking and some of the terrain, but this was his first outdoor climbing.
North Shore Rescue's own Facebook post (quoted by Gizmodo) says the hiker had somehow got far off the Crown hiking route and it was unclear exactly how or where.

Gizmodo recalls three hikers on California's Mount Shasta rescued this summer after relying heavily on Google's Gemini; the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office said Gemini advised far less food and water than the group needed.

Gizmodo says Markey recommends established tools such as Gaia GPS, CalTopo or AllTrails; CTV says North Shore Rescue was sent to Crown Mountain three times that weekend, unusual after years without a call there.
quote_evidence: A 16-year-old boy was rescued from steep mountainous terrain in the B.C. backcountry on Sunday after Claude AI guided him to the wrong location, according to North Shore Rescue.
Search Manager Paul Markey told CTV News that NSR members were called to the area of Crown Mountain, not far from Grouse Mountain, at around 3:30 p.m.
It remains unclear which AI tool the teen used to plan his route.
why_it_matters_hint: A teenager needed a helicopter rescue after following an AI-planned route; the rescue team warns against following AI route advice blindly, but the AI's role rests on its account.
event_date: Weekend of 3 and 4 Oct 2026 (Sunday 4 Oct per CTV News; Saturday 3 Oct per Gizmodo); first reported on 5 Oct 2026
notes: Credit follows the chain: Gizmodo relays North Shore News (not found), so the entry credits CTV News, which interviewed the rescue team's search manager itself and was read in full. The two outlets differ on the day (Saturday or Sunday) and on the tool (Gizmodo: unclear; CTV: Claude AI). The entry says 'over the weekend', names the tool as reported by CTV and notes Gizmodo's earlier uncertainty. The chatbot named is Claude, the model family of this writer, so the wording was kept strictly to the reports. Neither report publishes the AI conversation, and the rescue team itself said it was unclear exactly how he left the route. The event is before the window, so the entry is a follow-up of 4 Oct 2026 and the score is lowered by 1.
